name: Scattered Disc + Sednoids
story: Bodies on highly elliptical orbits beyond the Kuiper Belt — 50 to 1,000 AU. They were likely scattered out here by gravitational interactions with Neptune long ago. Sedna is the prototype Sednoid: 76 AU at perihelion, 937 AU at aphelion, an 11,400-year orbit. Their orbits are too far for Neptune to have placed them currently, hinting at influences from passing stars, a hypothetical Planet Nine, or the Sun's lost siblings from its birth cluster. No spacecraft has ever visited.
comparison: Sedna at aphelion sits 1/53rd of the way to the Sun's nearest stellar neighbour, Proxima Centauri. The light reaching Sedna from the Sun is 1/350,000th of what hits Earth.
